name: Jaipur
description: The Pink City — Rajasthan's capital and a UNESCO World Heritage Site known for its walled old city, Mughal-Rajput architecture, and vibrant bazaars.

name: Agra
description: Home to the Taj Mahal, Agra Fort, and Fatehpur Sikri — three UNESCO World Heritage Sites anchoring India's Mughal legacy.

name: Delhi
description: India's capital spans Old Delhi's Mughal monuments and New Delhi's colonial boulevards, offering thousands of years of layered history.

name: Varanasi
description: One of the world's oldest continuously inhabited cities. Sacred to Hindus, Buddhists, and Jains, known for its ghats, temples, and Ganga Aarti.

name: Udaipur
description: The City of Lakes — Rajasthan's most romantic city, famous for Lake Pichola, City Palace, and the Lake Palace hotel.

name: Mumbai
description: India's financial capital and most populous city — from Gateway of India and colonial South Mumbai to Bollywood studios and street food culture.

name: Amritsar
description: Spiritual home of Sikhism, home to the Golden Temple (Harmandir Sahib) and the historically significant Jallianwala Bagh.

name: Kochi
description: A port city where Chinese fishing nets, Dutch palaces, Jewish synagogues, and Portuguese churches share the waterfront of Fort Kochi.

name: Panaji
description: Goa's state capital — the gateway to the beach state's Portuguese heritage, colourful Fontainhas quarter, and Mandovi River.

name: Rishikesh
description: The Yoga Capital of the World — a Himalayan foothills town on the Ganges famous for ashrams, white-water rafting, and the Beatles Ashram.
